Behind the archive / Identity notes

A future,
in print.

Self-initiated
Portfolio concept

Design & development
Mustapha Fathiu

The Meridian Archive is an original visual identity and static website for an invented speculative-fiction author. It is a design study, not commissioned client work. Mara Vey, the novels, their excerpts and the essays are fictional.

One system, many worlds.

The art direction takes its cues from the printed futures of the 1970s: bold publishing typography, sun-faded colour, industrial geometry and generous editorial space. Split suns, nesting frames and contour lines form a small graphic vocabulary that changes meaning across each book.

Typography & colour.

Nimbus Sans carries the headlines and reading text. P052 Italic introduces a literary counterpoint. Nimbus Mono supplies the archive’s labels and coordinates. All fonts are hosted locally. Warm paper and near-black anchor the site; vermilion, olive and lavender distinguish its imagined worlds.

Space as structure.

A twelve-column desktop grid becomes a six-column intermediate layout and a single reading column on small screens. Uneven book positions and offset notes give way to a clear mobile sequence. Thin rules, generous margins and consistent metadata hold the pages together.

Built to travel.

The website uses semantic HTML, reusable CSS and a small vanilla JavaScript form enhancement. Original SVG artwork scales without a rendering service. Every page works on static hosting. No framework, build runtime, analytics or external asset request is required.

Honest interactions.

Book samples are original concept text. Signup and contact demonstrate browser validation and a visible local result. They do not send or store personal information. Navigation and reading remain available without JavaScript.
